column1: # Span R., Wagner W. (1996). A New Equation of State for Carbon Dioxide Covering the Fluid Region from the Triple-Point
# Temperature to 1100 K at Pressures up to 800 MPa. J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 25(6), 1509-1596. DOI 10.1063/1.555991.
# Source copy: NIST SRD reprint https://www.nist.gov/system/files/documents/srd/jpcrd516.pdf (scanned, no text layer),
# raw/span-wagner-1996-jpcrd-25-1509-nist-jpcrd516.pdf (sha256 85d732b0be26dc4736e8a768903e49e49e8ae6386447a93fd58bff6381544d34).
# Section 3.3, eq. (3.10), journal p.1520 (PDF page 12): melting pressure  p_m/p_t = 1 + a1 (T/T_t - 1) + a2 (T/T_t - 1)^2
# Section 3.4, eq. (3.12), journal p.1521 (PDF page 13): sublimation pressure
# T_t = 216.592 K, p_t = 0.51795 MPa for both. Both are constrained to the triple point by their form.
# Stated uncertainties: eq. (3.10) dp_m/p_m <= +-1.5 % for T_t <= T <= 225 K and <= +-0.5 % for 225 K < T <= 270 K;
# Eq. (3.12) was fitted to data above 154 K; below, the Bryson et al. data (70 to 103 K) deviate by no more than 0.01 Pa
# (T > 85 K) and 0.0001 Pa (T <= 85 K). Normal sublimation temperature from eq. (3.12): 194.6855 K (Bedford et al.:
# 194.6857 K +- 0.0030 K). Melting data: Michels et al. 1942 (217-266 K, to 284 MPa) and Clusius et al. 1960
# (217-222 K, to 24 MPa), temperatures corrected per eqs. (3.8)-(3.9).
# Local cross-check: CoolProp 8.0.0 CarbonDioxide.json (../coolprop/fluids/, identical to the worktree test resource
# src/test/resources/science/thermo/coolprop/CarbonDioxide.json, sha256 08e27e1a...5217) carries the melting line only:
